title: Bead crochet
subtitle: Stringing beads onto yarn before crocheting and incorporating them into stitches
excerpt: Bead crochet works by threading all the beads you will need onto the yarn before you start, then sliding each bead into position as you work the corresponding stitch. The bead is captured inside the stitch without any separate stringing or gluing.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Contemporary beading and crochet technique references.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique in which beads are pre-strung onto the working yarn, then slid into position as each stitch is formed, trapping the bead inside the stitch body.
Small uniform glass beads, typically 1–3 mm in diameter. Sold by size number: size 11 (small) through size 6 (large). The bead hole must be large enough for the working yarn to pass through twice.

content.text: puts beads into crochet fabric by pre-threading them onto the yarn before you start. Each bead slides into place as you work the stitch that holds it.
The method works best with fine crochet thread or smooth fingering-weight yarn and

. The critical question before starting is whether the thread can pass through the bead hole at least once. If the hole is too small for the thread, the project will not work. Thread size 10 crochet cotton fits most size 8 and size 6 seed beads. Size 11 beads need a finer thread.

items.name: Fine crochet cotton, size 10 or finer
items.note: The thread must fit through the bead hole. Test before buying a full project quantity.

items.name: Seed beads or small glass beads
items.note: Size 8 is a good starting point for size 10 thread. Pre-sort them: any bead with a blocked hole will jam on the thread mid-project.

items.name: Steel crochet hook, 1.0 mm or 1.5 mm
items.note: Sized to the thread, not to the beads

items.name: Big-eye beading needle
items.note: For threading beads onto the crochet cotton. The eye opens wide enough to accept thread; the whole needle passes through the bead.

items.name: Small dish or bead tray
items.note: To hold loose beads while threading

content.text: Count the total number of beads you need for the project and thread them all onto the yarn at the start. Thread in reverse pattern order: the last bead you will use goes on first, so that when you arrive at the stitch that needs it, the correct bead is ready at the back of the queue.
Thread the big-eye needle with the working thread. The needle body passes through the bead hole; pick up beads one at a time and slide them down the thread onto the yarn.
Push all threaded beads to the back of the yarn ball, away from the working end, until you need them.
Work to the stitch that will hold the first bead. Before completing the stitch, slide one bead along the thread to sit just behind the hook.
Begin the stitch: insert the hook, yarn over, draw up a loop. The bead sits on the loop between the hook and the working yarn.
Complete the stitch (yarn over, draw through both loops for a double crochet UK). The bead is now trapped on the front of the fabric.
Worked example: beaded foundation chain bracelet

A simple approach for a first bead crochet project: thread 20 beads onto the working thread. Make a chain long enough for a bracelet (approximately 20 cm). On the return row, place a bead in every other stitch. Fasten off and join the ends with a jump ring and clasp.

items.symptom: Beads are falling to the wrong side of the fabric
items.cause: The bead was slid into position after completing the yarn-over draw-through, rather than before.
items.fix: Slide the bead into position just before the final draw-through. The bead must be in place as the last loop is pulled to the front.

items.symptom: The thread broke when threading beads
items.cause: The thread was forced through a bead hole that was too small, or the bead had a rough edge that cut the fibre.
items.fix: Check bead hole size against thread diameter before threading. Discard any bead with a visible crack or sharp interior edge.

items.symptom: The fabric is twisting into a spiral
items.cause: Normal for bead crochet worked in continuous rounds. The bead placement angles slightly to one side as each round is worked.
items.fix: This is the expected result for tubular bead crochet ropes. Block the finished rope to straighten it slightly. To avoid the spiral, work in joined rounds rather than continuous spirals.

content.text: Once you are comfortable placing individual beads, a tubular bead crochet rope is the next step. Work 3 stitches in the round, placing a bead in each stitch, for a rope that is entirely bead-covered. These ropes can be finished as bracelets, necklaces, or bag straps.
